reviewer: Codex Standard scheduler follow-up implementation and semantic review
scope: Delta review against the retained Standard scheduling and glossary baseline. Changed source contracts and entire affected guide bodies were inspected; broad fingerprints detect future drift and do not certify unrelated modules anew.

domainReview.relay: Traced ordered first/live selection, reservation ownership, monotonic recovery gating, per-job quota notices/deadlines, reset-less observation retirement, completion/abort ordering, checkpoint recovery and delayed-lookup cancellation/freshness. Reviewed all changed guide bodies, rollout/rollback, actual running image, retained volume, 69 local checks and closed gates. Central custody, fixed-pool assignment, provider authorization, original request identity and Premium policy retain their existing contracts.
domainReview.images: Reviewed the complete shared queue guide against its baseline and the Standard-only scheduling delta. Application image receipts, free allowance, binary artifact publication and uncertain image replay are unchanged. Shared engine and public/auth regressions passed; no new database behavior or real provider image acceptance is claimed.

research.use: Per-host exclusion and bounded recovery pattern; no peer fallback or panic exception adopted.
Gradual return of traffic after recovery; adapted as a bounded local recovery-start rate, not Envoy weight ramping.
Rotation among available servers; adapted to account eligibility and one ongoing job per Standard account.

criticalReview: The changed critical watched input since the preceding review is QUEUE_SPECIFICATION.md. Inspected the whole queue contract and compiled boundary scan; package test-script changes retain their prior review. Explicit attestation and sync/check follow this retained review.
unmappedReview: Impact unmapped paths are generated navigation/catalog/inventory/review metadata, current-state operational index, and dated evidence records. No new unowned runtime source is present; Standard scheduler and fixtures are mapped in the existing relay domain.
limitations: No real provider sign-in, quota spend, generation, throughput measurement or public application deployment. Local empty-pool acceptance does not establish provider readiness.
Five seconds bounds new local recovery selections, not a provider quota. Long recovery jobs on different accounts can overlap if their selections are spaced by the interval.
The recovery budget, live rotation and central-denial history are process-local. Restart starts a new local budget; central ownership/grants and persisted provider cooldowns remain authoritative.
Checkpoint writes are best effort. Successful filesystem persistence is not an execution grant; no PostgreSQL schema, role, RLS policy or central budget change was made.
Request fairness does not imply equal token consumption. A sole healthy eligible account can receive consecutive completed jobs.
Monitor health remains centrally observed metadata, not live scheduler capacity. No browser UI or operator telemetry feed was added.
Cancellation avoidance applies before forwarding. Once forwarded, uncertain work retains its original key/account/epoch and cannot be repeated or moved.
Only Standard runtime was replaced. Premium, central and monitor image IDs retain their preceding pins. The trusted Mac remains the common physical host.
